newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Omnitel to be compensated in licence row.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Omnitel to be compensated in licence row.

text.p: The Italian government confirmed that the nation's second mobile phone group Omnitel would still be compensated for the licence fee that the company was forced to pay when it entered the cellular phone market.

The Italian Ministry of Post and Telecommunications issued a statement saying that Omnitel, controlled by Olivetti, would still be compensated after Post minister Antonio Maccanico met with Olivetti's chief executive Roberto Colaninno today.

Omnitel had complained to the European Commission about the 750 billion lire licence fee it was forced to pay when it started up its mobile phone service in 1995. Italy's other mobile player TIM majority-owned by state-controlled STET did not have to pay such a licence fee.

Under a compensation agreement, STET was to give Omnitel a 60 billion lire reduction in connection fees, but it appeared on Thursday that the government would not press ahead with this plan and STET would simply pay the state 120 billion lire.
The European Commission had supported Omnitel and Commissioner Karel Van Miert had written to Maccanico this week to complain that the 60 billion lire cut had not been made.
Maccanico told parliament on Thursday an alternative solution had been to ask STET to hand over to the state 120 billion lire to partly balance the Omnitel licence fee.
Olivetti's Colaninno said he was satisfied with the outcome of the meeting which had clarified the situation. (( -- Milan newsroom +392 66129502 ))
